title: feature-telemetry-matrix-and-trace-anchors-wip
body:
Purpose:
This is a working doc to capture a feature-focused telemetry matrix and a concise tracing anchor plan for rollout windows. Goal: ensure every new serving feature (variant routing, prefix cache, dynamic batching, fallback routing) ships with a minimum set of signals + a tracing anchor design so we can detect regressions and explain latency spikes quickly.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: SRE, serving runtime, product, QE.
- Scope: hosted + dedicated runtime paths for tokenized inference. Private deployments are out-of-scope for the first pass (we will adapt later).

Why a matrix?
We keep seeing gaps: e.g., team ships a batching change but metrics only include end-to-end latency; root cause (queueing vs kernel dispatch) is unclear. The matrix ties feature flows to observable primitives and required spans.

High-level telemetry primitives (required across features):
- request_id (trace_id propagation)
- model_id, model_variant, seq_len_estimate, route_policy
- token_streamed_count (for streaming requests)
- cpu_ms and gpu_ms per request (where available)
- queue_time_ms, batch_wait_ms, kernel_dispatch_ms, decode_ms
- kv_cache_hit (bool) and kv_cache_hit_rate (per-key / per-prefix)
- fallback_reason (string tag) and fallback_count
- retry_count, client_timeout_flag
- error_type (parser/model/runtime) and http_status

Telemetry matrix (feature -> minimum metrics + nice-to-have):
1) Dynamic batching (autoscale/batcher):
  - must: request_count, batch_size_distribution (p10/p50/p90), queue_time_ms, end_to_end_latency_p95, dropped_requests
  - nice: kernel_dispatch_ms_by_batch_size, batch_utilization_ratio, batch_formation_rate
  - trace anchors: span:batch.wait, span:batch.form, span:kernel.dispatch

2) Prefix/KV cache: 
  - must: kv_cache_lookup_total, kv_cache_hit_total, kv_cache_miss_latency_ms, cache_hit_rate_by_prefix
  - nice: memory_pressure_by_cache_shard, cache_eviction_events, cache_fill_time_ms
  - trace anchors: span:kv.lookup -> tag:kv.key_hash, span:kv.apply

3) Fallback routing & model variant switch: 
  - must: fallback_count, fallback_rate_by_model, fallback_latency_delta, fallback_reason_tags
  - nice: capacity_utilization_primary, cold_start_time_ms_secondary
  - trace anchors: span:route.resolve, span:model.load (if cold), span:model.fallback

4) Streaming (server-sent tokens):
  - must: token_emit_rate, downstream_write_latency_ms, open_stream_count, stream_error_count
  - nice: stream_backpressure_events, dropped_token_events, client_rtt_ms
  - trace anchors: span:stream.open, span:stream.chunk.write, span:stream.close

Tracing anchors and design conventions (proposal):
- Top-level trace_id = request_id. Every request should produce a minimal trace with these root-level spans (naming exact strings):
  1) http.receive (root)
  2) proto.parse (if payload heavy)
  3) route.resolve (decide model/variant/region) -> tag:route_policy
  4) batch.wait (if batching used) -> tag:batch_id, batch_size
  5) kernel.dispatch (includes GPU op timing) -> tag:gpu_id, kernel_name
  6) kv.lookup (if cache used) -> tag:kv_hit=true/false, kv_key_hash
  7) decode (tokenize/detokenize) -> tag:input_tokens/output_tokens
  8) stream.write (if streaming) -> tag:chunk_size
- All spans should include: request_id, model_id, model_variant, customer_id (if applicable), region, stage (hosted/dedicated/private) as tags.
- Sampling policy: default tail-based adaptive sampling: retain 100% of error traces; retain 100% of traces with latency > p99 of that route/model; sample normal traces at 0.5% per route, adjustable per-SLO. This keeps storage bounded but ensures we have problem traces.

Dashboard layout notes (high level layout for rollout page):
Panel row 1 (global health): global request rate, global e2e latency p50/p95/p99, global error rate, SLO burn rate (7d), current incidents
Row 2 (workload slices): e2e latency heatmap by model_variant and seq_len_bucket (1-64,65-256,257-1024), token rate by customer tier, batch_size distribution heatmap
Row 3 (root-cause anchors): queue_time_ms timeseries, kernel_dispatch_ms timeseries, kv_cache_hit_rate timeseries, fallback_rate timeseries (annotate rollout events)
Row 4 (traces & examples): recent sampled traces table (searchable by request_id), top 10 slowest traces, error traces grouped by error_type
Row 5 (postmortem helpers): recent deploys (time-series annotate), canary vs stable comparison charts (latency, error, cost), and quick links to rollback runbooks and PRs

Alerting and thresholds (suggested):
- P0: error rate > 0.5% over 5m AND error_count increase 5x from baseline -> page oncall, auto-open INC
- P1: e2e latency p99 > 2x baseline for 15m -> notify SRE + owning eng team
- P2: kv_cache_hit_rate drop by >= 20% relative to 1h baseline -> slack alert to cache owners
- Canary guardrails: if canary p95 latency > stable p95 by 25% for 10m -> auto-fail canary and page

Instrumentation checklist (PR template additions):
- [ ] Add span roots with canonical names listed above
- [ ] Emit request_id as top-level header / tag and propagate to downstream services
- [ ] Emit metric counters / histograms with suffixes: _count, _latency_ms, _ratio where applicable
- [ ] Add experiment/rollout tags (canary=true/false, rollout_id)
- [ ] Unit tests for histogram bucketing and example metrics for synthetic requests
- [ ] End-to-end synthetic test that asserts trace anchors appear in sampled traces

Regression detection and variance rules (quick heuristics):
- Track rolling baselines by route and seq_len_bucket (1h, 6h, 24h) and compute drift score = weighted z-score across latency, error, and token_rate. If drift_score > threshold, create automated issue in tracking board and attach 5 sample traces.
- Use correlation matrix: if e2e latency increases and kernel_dispatch_ms correlates >= 0.6, flag kernel path; if queue_time_ms correlates >= 0.6, flag batching/queueing.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How do we capture GPU stall time separately from kernel dispatch for multi-kernel models? Need additional exporter fields from runtime (gpu_busy_ms vs kernel_dispatch_ms).
- Tail sampling vs cost: we need a forecast for trace storage at proposed sampling rates per 1M requests/day. Miguel to follow up with cost estimate (INF-321).
- Private deployments: plan to provide the same span naming but allow customers to opt-out of trace upload; will need local aggregation and log-only mode.

Next steps and owner action items:
- Asha: finalize canonical span names and publish to confluence (target 2026-02-22)
- Miguel: cost projection for sampling policy and storage model (due 2026-03-01)
- Priya: add telemetry checklist to PR template and create example instrumentation PR in repo (target 2026-02-27)
- Follow-up sync scheduled: Observability sync 2026-02-25, 10:30 PT (agenda: finalize spans, agree sampling, dashboard draft)

Appendix: quick example queries (pseudo-promql / pseudo-sql):
- cache_hit_rate = sum(kv_cache_hit_total) by (model_variant) / sum(kv_cache_lookup_total) by (model_variant)
- batch_wait_p95 = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(batch_wait_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- e2e_p99_by_seq = histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(e2e_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, seq_len_bucket))

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive — the goal is low-friction onboarding for features so that any rollout has the minimum visibility to detect user-facing regressions quickly. Expect iteration and follow-ups.
